response.body:
Related to #2140.

The directory picker can return an exception when persisting its URI grant or inspecting the selected document. Both settings and setup currently await `pickDirectory()` outside their error-handling block, so those failures can escape the lifecycle coroutine instead of reaching the existing failure feedback.

Include directory selection in the existing error boundary. Keep cancellation silent, rethrow lifecycle `CancellationException`, and retain the existing distinction between first-time external-sync setup and replacing a saved directory. Settings no longer needs a second launch on the same lifecycle scope.

This does not implement upgrade migration or change the synchronization algorithm. The reporter's old upgrade failure has not been reproduced; #2140 is related, not claimed fully fixed. It is independent of the confirmation UI in #2199.

Validation:

- [All five CI checks](https://github.com/osfans/trime/actions/runs/40685899028) passed: lint/unit tests and four OS builds. The actual Ubuntu producer is synthetic merge `6168da40`; its complete Git tree matches head `f45ba68d`.
- Android 15 emulator A/B checks covered the settings and setup entry points. A test monitor returned a synthetic picker result with an ungranted URI, exercising the real `StorageAccess` result parser and permission request. Both baseline entry points crashed with the uncaught `SecurityException`. Each fixed entry point displayed the existing failure feedback and allowed a second attempt. The inspected mode/URI, retained read/write grants, sync-manifest bytes and private sentinel stayed unchanged during these pre-persistence failures. Setup's empty-URI fixture was prepared explicitly.
- 54 extracted-function JVM control-flow checks with stub dependencies and real coroutines covered null results, failures, cancellation and success. These are diagnostic checks, separate from the application CI and Android execution.

The emulator used local-certificate diagnostic copies; all 784 non-signature APK entries were verified identical to their CI originals. This was an injected result and accessibility-action test, not a real provider-failure reproduction, physical-device, release-signature or upgrade test. Early harness/navigation failures and emulator boot ANRs were retained; CI tool/native-dependency warnings remain.

The patch does not add transaction rollback after a valid selection has already been persisted and synchronization subsequently fails. First-time APP-to-external setup still uses the existing fallback policy. These limits, and the unverified historical upgrade cause, are why this is **Related to #2140**, not a closing fix.
response.title: fix(storage): handle folder picker failures without swallowing cancellation
